stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the orange source along its dashed track. Watch the ray cross the air-water interface — the ratio $n_1 \sin(i_1) / (n_2 \sin(i_2))$ stays at $1$.
stages.concept: Snell-Descartes law: $n_1 \sin(i_1) = n_2 \sin(i_2)$. Going from air ($n_1 = 1.00$) into water ($n_2 = 1.33$), the ray bends toward the normal, so $i_2 < i_1$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Aim the source, then press Fire (or Space) to shoot. Light all 3 underwater targets — you have 7 shots.
stages.concept: Snell's law lets you predict where the beam surfaces under water. If you want the refracted ray to reach a target, solve $\sin(i_1) = (n_2 / n_1) \sin(i_2)$ for the required $i_1$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The refracted ray is hidden. Read the coordinates of $S$, $I$ and $T$, compute the incident angle $i_1$ that lands the beam on the target, place $S$, then Fire. Peek gives you the strategy.
stages.concept: For each target, compute $i_2 = \arctan((T_x - I_x) / (I_y - T_y))$, then invert Snell: $\sin(i_1) = (n_2 / n_1) \sin(i_2)$. Place $S$ so the incident ray from $S$ to $I$ has that angle from the vertical normal.

labels.exhausted: OUT OF SHOTS · RESET TO RETRY
labels.tip1: drag the source to change i₁
labels.tip2: aim, then press SPACE to fire
labels.tip3: compute i₁ from Snell, place S, then fire
labels.tir: TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION · NO REFRACTED RAY
labels.peek_strategy: invert snell: sin(i₁) = (n₂/n₁)·sin(i₂). read T-I to get i₂ first.

1.1: Grab the orange source and slide it across the dashed track.
1.2: As you slide, watch the incident angle i₁ and the refracted angle i₂ in the corner readout — one is always smaller than the other.
1.3: Water is denser than air (n₂ > n₁), so the ray bends toward the normal on entering water: i₂ < i₁ always.

2.1: The beam fires only when you press Fire (or Space). Aim first by placing the source.
2.2: To hit a target T beneath the water, the refracted ray from I must go through T. Compute i₂ from the T-to-I direction, then use Snell to get the incident angle i₁ you need at the surface.
2.3: Sign check: if T is to the right of I, the source S must be to the LEFT of I (the ray bends but does not flip sides at the interface).

3.1: Write down S, I and T coordinates from the scene labels — you'll need them all.
3.2: Step 1: from T and I, compute i₂ = arctan((T.x − I.x) / (I.y − T.y)) in Cartesian y-up. Step 2: sin(i₁) = (n₂ / n₁) · sin(i₂) — take arcsin to get i₁.
3.3: Step 3: place S at S.x = I.x − sign(T.x − I.x) · (I.y − S.y) · tan(i₁), where I.y − S.y = 125 in Cartesian. Peek shows the current i₁ so you can verify before firing.
